status: Original early Stop recovery verified in both modes after file completion; complete command recovery remains in progress

shared_implementation.native: Namespace original owner context and file receipts; Host.recover_original_control and Journal.complete reuse original ownership and outcome publication
shared_implementation.backend: OriginalCommandRequest, recovery_authority.verify and Store.original_language_command share one recovery-only callback policy
shared_implementation.adapters: Service and paired file transports retain their original callback at admission; recovery uses the same pinned OriginalCommandJournal above HTTP primitives
shared_implementation.locking: A bounded process-local FIFO queues lock attempts by the original anchor object. OS locks continue to coordinate processes. Queue and filesystem acquisition share the original wait budget.

behavior: Persist the original issuer secret, callback origin and immutable scope binding in bounded private owner metadata; reconstruct authority without copying large provider/source payloads into fixed command-result space.

Record positive original file completion while holding the complete physical folder lease, before releasing file credentials. Unknown legacy effects and unfinished file work cannot justify no-dispatch cleanup.
Observe or clean up only with the original issuer and reserved command worker. Reject browser transport, substituted identities and every Claim, including structurally valid Start and Recover.

Stop a reserved, never-dispatched command after original file completion even when no original LSP session exists. Persist its native rejection before publication; retain exclusion through manual acknowledgement and exact backend/native settlement.
Retry exact rejection and final settlement acknowledgements through shared storage CAS. Preserve the original outcome and forbid replay.

Avoid unchanged owner/result/receipt publications and repeated validation of the same locked database snapshot. Keep original object, namespace, schema, digest, revision and directory-flush checks; prevent fresh local readers from starving a waiting publisher.
behavioral_tests: Both-mode HTTP matrix: success, Stop before Start, Stop from a fresh host with no original LSP session, Git branch change and branch round trip. All ten scenarios retain original result/file assertions, await settlement and run an ordinary native command through the physical folder gate afterward.

Original callback HTTP policy in both modes: forbidden browser headers, forged issuer, wrong project, wrong private worker, valid Start/Recover envelopes, unfinished file work, valid compact reads and transport-secret rotation.

Storage in both modes: reserved Approved cleanup after actual file worker release and provider revocation, exact lost rejection ACK, manual acknowledgement, lost final settlement ACK, original terminal observation and idle project state.

Native namespace: original credential and origin survive reopen; unfinished work cannot be rejected; complete file receipt survives reopen while retaining command exclusion; different callback is rejected; legacy upgrade keeps unknown effects; context corruption and schema downgrade are rejected.

An actual shared OS reader holds the anchor while an exclusive publisher queues. A later reader cannot pass that publisher. All original native busy-initializer, persistence, object replacement, cleanup and recovery assertions remain enabled under default parallelism.

verification.qualification: The final native-only changes affect four private native bridge files. The eight successful shared cases retain identical non-bridge package/build inputs; earlier native failures remain recorded as failures. All affected native checks were rerun on the final code.

limits: The fresh-host HTTP case creates a new server/host and session registry in the same test process against the same private namespace. It does not prove an abrupt OS-process crash or packaged-app restart.

Controls can observe an already-recorded native outcome, but do not yet restart its failed publisher after host loss. Startup reconciliation, watcher completion receipts and history-pruned final-ACK recovery remain unfinished.
Early Cancel retirement and callback rebinding with a fresh original-scope proof remain unfinished. Unknown legacy context stays pending rather than inferring cleanup.
Lost-ACK assertions here are shared storage contracts, not injected HTTP connection failures. Complete transport fault and phase-lifetime coverage remains required.
Direct backend/WASI writer participation, native Windows ownership, fresh Linux and packaged-app checks, all required CI, and all original cache/resource/prefetch requirements remain open.
